children.name: restart.note
children.text: You go back to the entrance and every puzzle in here resets: gates, plates, echoes and anything you were carrying for the doors. Rewards you already took, and lanterns you lit, are still yours.

children.name: end.body
children.text: Thistledown is written in, and the Margin Gate stands open. Whatever lies beyond it will have to wait for the next chapter.

children.name: book.text0
children.text: Every world begins as someone's idea, written in a hurry, mostly in pencil.

children.name: book.text1
children.text:
Writing a world is the easy part. Keeping it is harder. For that there have always been Storytenders: small, patient people who live in the margins and look after whatever the author forgot.

They mend plot holes. They remember the minor characters. They read the unfinished parts aloud, so those parts know somebody is listening.

children.name: book.text2
children.text: Once there were thousands. Then the Editors arrived, with red pens and very large scissors and a firm belief that less is more. Behind them came the Redaction: a white that eats everything, and is awfully tidy about it.

children.name: book.text3
children.text:
Now there is one left. Well. One doodle. In the margin of page forty-one, somebody sketched a small figure holding a lantern, and was then called to dinner.

Nobody finished the drawing. Nobody gave it a job.

children.name: book.text4
children.text:
That is where you come in. You are not part of the main plot, which is exactly why the Redaction cannot quite see you.

And you love this flawed, half-finished world. Somebody ought to.

children.name: map.none
children.text: Light a lantern post out in the world, and you can travel to it from here.
